text: Strands Agents runs a model-driven loop: the model decides whether to answer or call a tool, the tool result is fed back, and the cycle repeats until the model decides it is finished. The framework owns reliability of the loop, not the control flow.
LangGraph asks the developer to define control flow explicitly as nodes, edges, and conditional branches. The reasoning path is a graph you wrote and can inspect step by step.
Bedrock AgentCore provides identity, memory, and runtime for agents, including IAM-based permissions on individual tools and built-in session management.
A tool-calling loop that never terminates is usually a prompt problem, not a framework problem. Setting a maximum iteration count is the cheapest guardrail against runaway agent cost.
HNSW builds a navigable small-world graph over vectors. Recall is tuned with ef_search at query time and ef_construction at index time; higher values trade latency for accuracy.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores magnitude, which is why normalized embeddings behave predictably under it.
Approximate nearest neighbour search trades exactness for speed. An exact k-NN scan is still the right answer for small collections where a full pass costs less than maintaining a graph index.
The dimension declared in a knn_vector mapping must match the embedding model output exactly. A model swap that changes dimension requires a full reindex, not a configuration change.
Chroma runs embedded in the application process or as a lightweight local server, backed by hnswlib. There is no cluster to provision before the first query.
Chroma is released under the Apache 2.0 licence, so self-hosting carries no software cost. The only spend is the compute it runs on.
A PersistentClient writes the collection to local disk, which survives process restarts but not the loss of the machine. There is no built-in replication.
Chroma is code-first and ships no dashboard of its own. Inspecting collection size, distance distribution, or query behaviour means writing your own scripts.
OpenSearch began as a full-text search engine built on Lucene, and gained vector search through the k-NN plugin. That lineage is why a single query can combine BM25 and vector similarity.
OpenSearch Dashboards ships with the service and provides cluster health, shard status, and a query console without any additional setup.
A hybrid query needs a search pipeline with a normalization processor. BM25 and k-NN produce scores on incompatible scales, and without normalization there is nothing to combine them with.

OpenSearch Serverless collections require an encryption policy, a network policy, and a data access policy. A missing data access policy produces a 403 that is easy to mistake for a credentials error.
Requests to a Serverless collection are signed with SigV4 against the aoss service name. A managed OpenSearch domain uses es instead, and the wrong value fails without a useful message.
OpenSearch Serverless bills in OpenSearch Compute Units. Capacity has a floor, so an idle collection still accrues cost for every hour it exists.
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases uses OpenSearch Serverless as its default vector store, which makes OpenSearch the path of least resistance for retrieval inside Bedrock.
Foundation models must be enabled per account under Model access before they can be invoked. A model that has not been enabled returns an AccessDeniedException rather than a descriptive error.
Titan Text Embeddings V2 returns 1024 dimensions by default and can also emit 256 or 512. Titan Text Embeddings V1 is fixed at 1536 dimensions.
Chunk size is a retrieval decision, not a formatting one. Chunks that are too large dilute the embedding; chunks that are too small lose the context that made the passage meaningful.
Semantic search alone struggles with exact identifiers such as error codes, product SKUs, and acronyms like IAM, where a user expects a literal keyword match rather than a paraphrase.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines two result lists using rank position rather than raw score, which makes it a portable way to merge keyword and vector results when score normalization is unavailable.
